elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on thirty (30) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 specifies thirty (30) days' prior notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly requires prior written notice to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination becomes effective.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires Vendor to refund all prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination, which operates as the required pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly states that Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.
Section 9.4 expressly grants Customer a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: The required notice period for Customer's termination for convenience is at least 60 days.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires only thirty (30) days' prior notice, not the fallback minimum of 60 days.

elements.element: The required notice period for Customer's termination for convenience does not exceed 90 days.
elements.evidence: The specified thirty (30)-day notice period does not exceed 90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee imposed on Customer for termination for convenience does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 prohibits any penalty or early-termination fee, so the conditional fee cap is satisfied at zero.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience may become effective only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right is granted, and Section 9.4 expressly bars Vendor from terminating for convenience during a term; therefore no such termination may become effective before term end.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered language grants Vendor no termination-for-convenience right. Because the conditional trigger is demonstrably absent, no Vendor exercise exists for which a 90-day notice protection is required.

result.reason: The redline fully satisfies the preferred position through an operative 30-day written-notice right, a refund of prepaid post-termination fees, and an express prohibition on Vendor convenience termination during a term. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its 60-day minimum Customer notice period is absent. The drafting is clear and preserves the existing for-cause rights, but it is not strictly minimal because the added right to terminate “in whole or in part” expands Customer's rights beyond what either stated position requires.
